long_biography.plain_text:
Treatment access shaped Raphaella Warwick’s research into mindfulness support for parents of children with developmental disabilities. Her work asked why families experiencing psychological distress can struggle to secure help, identifying cost, childcare and scarce providers as practical obstacles.

Warwick carried that question into intervention design. She examined a brief mindfulness programme delivered online, reducing the time and travel demands of face-to-face care. Participants reported improvements in mood and mindfulness that were maintained at follow-up, though recruitment remained difficult. Her research joins clinical efficacy with a practical concern: whether psychological support can be designed around the constraints already borne by parents.
